name: Parkinson's Disease
summary: Parkinson's disease is a progressive neurodegenerative disease caused by loss of dopamine-producing neurons in the substantia nigra. Dopamine helps the basal ganglia produce smooth, well-scaled, automatic movement.

Difficulty turning in bed, rising from a chair.
Falls, often while turning or multitasking.

blocks.text: Parkinson's disease is a progressive neurodegenerative disease caused by loss of dopamine-producing neurons in the substantia nigra. Dopamine helps the basal ganglia produce smooth, well-scaled, automatic movement. Its loss produces the four cardinal motor features and many non-motor symptoms.

rows: Slowness and progressive reduction in movement size
Increased resistance throughout passive range ("lead pipe", or "cogwheel" with tremor)
"Pill-rolling" tremor at rest, often one-sided at onset
Impaired balance reactions, later in the disease

blocks.text: Non-motor: constipation, low mood, anxiety, sleep problems, reduced smell, orthostatic hypotension, cognitive change, pain.

**Hoehn and Yahr stages**: 1 one-sided; 2 both sides, balance intact; 3 balance impairment, independent; 4 severe disability, can still walk or stand unassisted; 5 wheelchair or bed bound unless aided.

sections.title: B. Recognize the presentation for physiotherapy

items: Shuffling gait with short steps, reduced arm swing, stooped posture.
Freezing of gait: feet feel "glued" at doorways, turns, starting, or in crowded places.
Difficulty turning in bed, rising from a chair.
Falls, often while turning or multitasking.

blocks.text: Time since diagnosis; medication timings and how long each dose lasts; freezing (the New Freezing of Gait Questionnaire); falls and near falls; activities difficult at home; dizziness on standing; mood, cognition; exercise history.

blocks.label: TEACHER'S VOICE
body: Book therapy sessions during the patient's "on" period (about 45 to 60 minutes after medication) for learning new skills. Assess during "off" periods too if falls happen then.

sections.title: D to E. Examination and measures

rows: Motor examination (done by trained clinicians) [Ref – to verify]
Timed Up and Go (and with a cognitive dual task)
Postural reactions: stand behind, give a quick backward pull; more than two steps or no step indicates impairment [Ref – to verify]

sections.title: G. RED FLAGS AND URGENT CONDITIONS

rows: Sudden severe rigidity, fever, confusion after stopping medication

steps: **Early stage (H&Y 1 to 2):** promote exercise: aerobic, strength, large-amplitude movement, balance. Prevent inactivity.
**Middle stage (H&Y 2 to 4):** add falls prevention, cueing strategies for freezing, transfers, dual-task training.
**Late stage (H&Y 5):** maintain transfers, prevent complications, train carers, positioning.

rows: Practise large, exaggerated whole-body movements repeatedly; "think big"
Visual (lines on the floor, laser cane), auditory (metronome or music at a set beat), verbal ("big step")
Stop, weight shift side to side, step over a real or imaginary line, march to a count, turn in a wide arc
Getting out of a chair or bed
Break the task into steps and practise each consciously
Progressive balance training, including dual tasks and perturbations
Aerobic exercise at moderate to high intensity (treadmill, cycling, dance, boxing-style programs)
Progressive resistance training for legs and trunk extensors

blocks.label: MEMORY HOOK
body: Parkinson's makes movement automatic movement fail. Strategies work by making movement conscious and cued.

blocks.text: Not central. Assistive devices (wheeled walkers, laser cues) chosen carefully: some walkers may increase freezing in certain patients [Ref – to verify].
TUG, Mini-BESTest, gait speed, step length, freezing questionnaire, falls diary, quality of life (PDQ-39).

items: **Why schedule therapy during "on" periods?** The patient moves and learns better when medication is effective.
**How do auditory cues help?** They provide an external rhythm that bypasses impaired internal timing.
**What should a patient do when freezing at a doorway?** Stop, shift weight, then step over a target line or march to a count.
**Why is exercise important even in early disease?** It improves fitness, function and may slow functional decline.
**Fever, severe rigidity and confusion after missing medication?** Possible parkinsonism-hyperpyrexia syndrome: emergency.

sections.title: Now You Should Be Able To

items: Describe the motor and non-motor features of Parkinson's disease.
Plan stage-appropriate exercise and falls prevention.
